input: Write a postcard to my pen pal in Oslo

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing who the pen pal is — a close friend, a new acquaintance, someone of a different age — shapes the warmth, formality, and assumptions the message can make.
The occasion or trigger for writing (a holiday, a recent trip, just keeping in touch) determines what the postcard is anchored around and what news to share.
A postcard has very limited space; knowing which specific topics or updates to include (and exclude) prevents a vague or overloaded message.
The desired tone — warm and casual, witty and playful, poetic — fundamentally changes word choice, sentence rhythm, and how the message feels to read.
Whether this is a physical postcard (with strict character limits and a chosen image) or a digital/e-postcard affects format, length, and what the final deliverable looks like.
Knowing what the user wants the pen pal to feel or do after reading — feel connected, laugh, reply about a specific topic — clarifies what a well-done message achieves.
Any hard limits such as word count, language (English vs. Norwegian), or things to avoid (sensitive topics, oversharing) directly constrain what can be written.

gold.taskTitle: Write a postcard to pen pal in Oslo
gold.taskDescription: Draft a postcard message for the user to send to their pen pal who lives in Oslo, Norway.

questions.title: How well do you know this pen pal so far?
questions.description: Establish the closeness and history of the relationship — new pen pal, months of letters, childhood friend — so the message can match the right level of familiarity.

questions.title: What is prompting you to write right now?
questions.description: Identify the occasion or trigger — a holiday, a recent experience, a reply to their last letter, or just a spontaneous check-in — to give the postcard a clear anchor.

questions.title: What one or two things do you most want to mention?
questions.description: Pin down the specific content to include, such as a trip, a funny moment, a question for them, or local news, so the limited postcard space is used well.

questions.title: What tone should the message have — warm, witty, or poetic?
questions.description: Clarify the stylistic feel the user wants, since this shapes every word choice and determines whether the postcard feels like a cosy note, a joke, or a lyrical snapshot.

questions.title: Is this a physical postcard or a digital message?
questions.description: Determine the format so the draft respects real physical space constraints (roughly 40-60 words) or can be a little longer and richer for a digital format.

questions.title: How do you want your pen pal to feel after reading it?
questions.description: Define the emotional outcome — connected, curious, amused, warmly missed — so the closing lines and overall message are shaped toward that specific effect.

questions.title: Should it be written in English or another language?
questions.description: Confirm the language of the postcard, since writing in Norwegian, mixing languages, or sticking to English are all valid choices that completely change what gets drafted.
